ruleName: Relief for Ball in Penalty Area
imagePrompt: Illustrate a golf course scene featuring a penalty area clearly marked with yellow stakes along the edge of a water hazard. Show a golfer in modern golf attire, standing close to this edge, thoughtfully holding a golf ball as if preparing for a drop. The original ball should be visible inside the yellow-staked penalty area near the edge. Use a polished, modern, semi-realistic illustration style: 75% realistic and 25% stylised. Do not include any text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles. There should be no red stakes anywhere in the scene.
imageAlt: A golfer stands near a water hazard marked by yellow stakes, holding a ball and appearing to decide about relief, with the original ball visible just inside the penalty area.

sceneSpec.setting: Golf course, edge of a water hazard marked with yellow stakes
sceneSpec.players: One player, dressed in typical golf clothing, preparing to take relief
sceneSpec.ballPosition: Ball has just entered and come to rest inside a yellow-staked penalty area, visible just inside the marked hazard
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: Player is considering dropping a ball within two club-lengths of the yellow penalty area's edge for lateral relief
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Highlight the difference in relief options between yellow and red penalty areas
mustShow: Yellow stakes marking the edge of a water penalty area
A player near the edge, with ball clearly in the penalty area
Player in a thoughtful or decision-making pose, holding a ball ready to drop
mustNotShow: Arrows, numbers or lines showing relief area
Any text, labels, badges, logos, scorecards, diagrams, captions or speech bubbles

questions.title: Can You Drop to the Side from a Yellow Penalty Area?
questions.question: Your ball lands in a yellow penalty area (like a pond with yellow stakes). Can you drop your ball to the side (within two club-lengths) from where it went in?

choices.text: Yes. You can always drop to the side from any penalty area.
Yes, but only if you can’t find your ball.
No. You can only drop to the side if the penalty area has red stakes.
Yes, but only if you add two penalty shots.

questions.explanation: If you see yellow stakes or lines, you cannot drop your ball to the side. Dropping to the side (lateral relief) is only for red penalty areas. For yellow penalty areas, you have to drop farther back in line with the flag or go back and play another ball.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Parts of the course marked with yellow or red stakes or lines, often with water or mud, where special rules apply.
Dropping the ball to the side, not back, after it goes into trouble.

questions.teachingTip: Show children the different colour stakes on the course and help them remember what to do for red and yellow penalty areas.
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking you can always drop to the side no matter the stake colour.
Believing the same relief options apply for yellow and red penalty areas.

questions.title: Lateral Relief from Yellow Penalty Area
questions.question:
Your ball comes to rest in a yellow-staked penalty area. You would like to take lateral relief by dropping within two club-lengths of where the ball last crossed the edge of the penalty area.

Is this allowed?

choices.text: Yes. You may always take lateral relief from any penalty area.
Yes, but only if the ball cannot be found.
No. Lateral relief is only available from a red penalty area.
Yes, but only if you add two penalty strokes.

questions.explanation: Lateral relief (dropping within two club-lengths of where the ball last crossed the edge) is available only from red penalty areas. For yellow penalty areas, you may take stroke-and-distance relief or back-on-the-line relief, both for one penalty stroke. Lateral relief is not allowed from a yellow penalty area under Rule 17.1d.
